title: Identify your backflow preventer before you troubleshoot it
description: Use visible features and installation context to separate RPZ, double-check, pressure vacuum breaker, and look-alike devices.
prompt: Which description is closest to what you can see?
answer: A backflow preventer protects a water supply from reverse flow, but different assemblies fail, drain, and require testing in different ways.
urgency: Do not open a sealed assembly or bypass it. If water is continuous, forceful, freezing, or flooding the area, move to the leak safety path.
diagramAlt: Simplified RPZ backflow preventer diagram with two shutoff valves and a lower relief vent
identifiers: A relief opening beneath the body usually points to an RP or RPZ assembly.
A raised bonnet or air inlet above the piping often points to a pressure vacuum breaker.
Two check modules without an open relief vent may point to a double-check assembly.

choices.label: Water is leaking or discharging
choices.detail: Start with where the water exits and when it happens.

choices.label: I received a test notice
choices.detail: Understand the test and then verify the local utility rule.

choices.label: The device failed a test
choices.detail: Repair is only one part of closing the record.

choices.label: I am deciding whether to repair or replace
choices.detail: Compare body damage, repairable internals, retest, and total job scope.

steps.title: Read the nameplate
steps.body: Record the manufacturer, model, size, and any RP, RPZ, PVB, DC, or AVB marking.

steps.title: Locate the air or relief opening
steps.body: The location of an intentional opening is a stronger clue than the overall brass shape.

steps.title: Note the system
steps.body: Irrigation, fire line, domestic water, hose connection, and sewer piping do not use interchangeable devices.

safeChecks: Photograph the whole assembly and the nameplate.
Note exactly where water appears without removing covers.
Keep the utility notice or prior test report beside the device.
stopConditions: Continuous discharge that can flood or freeze
A cracked or visibly distorted body
A fire-protection or commercial life-safety connection
Any instruction that would require bypassing the assembly
notThisDevice: A bell-shaped pressure regulator controls downstream pressure; it is not a backflow preventer.
A sewer backwater valve blocks wastewater reversal and belongs to a separate system.
A hose-bib vacuum breaker is a small atmospheric device at a faucet, not a testable RPZ assembly.

related.title: Find the utility named on the notice

evidenceNote: Identification guidance is national and observational. Testing, repair authorization, and reporting requirements must be verified with the governing utility.
